map.An Axiom City episode — Lessons 4-1 & 4-: An Axiom City episode — Lessons 4-1 & 4-2 in one sitting, with three gates. Solve the math to move the story.
map.Market status: opens in ten minutes. Pie: The market opens in ten minutes. The pier is cracked in three places. The crew is holding one hundred lanterns. Carefully.
map.Previously: on a rained-out field day, f: Last time: on a rainy field day, four sixth graders woke VEX in the old observatory. VEX is a piece of Ada Vex's Pattern Engine. Then the autumn storm broke the old pier. Tonight the Night Market opens to save it. Every stall, every lantern, every coin helps pay for the repair.
map.The waterfront, dusk. Stalls glowing, cr: The waterfront at dusk. The stalls glow. The crowd arrives. Hana and Eliot struggle to lift one very important board up a ladder.
map.Easy — EASY! One hundred lanterns, ten r: Easy, EASY! One hundred lanterns, ten rows of ten. This board IS the fundraiser, Eliot. Drop it and we lose the pier.
map.Relax, I've hauled rarer loot through wo: Relax. I have carried rare loot through worse maps. It is a giant progress bar. Every donation block lights one lantern.
map.The board goes up over the square. An ho: The board goes up over the square. One hour into the market, the first donation blocks arrive.
map.Ms. Ortiz pledged the first blocks — twe: Ms. Ortiz gave the first blocks. Twenty-five lanterns are lit already. Twenty-five out of one hundred.
So the board does the math just by being there. 25 out of 100 is also the decimal 0.25. Same amount, different costume. But the PERCENT number is 25. No decimal point.
map.Definition loaded: a percent is a rate p: Definition: a percent is a rate per hundred. 25 out of 100 = 25%. The symbol % means "out of 100" for you. Write the count, add the sign, done.
map.Reader — you're our fifth crew member. T: Reader, you are our fifth crew member. The donation rush is here and the crowd wants numbers. Read the boards. Post the percents.
map.Hana's board holds 100 lanterns in a 10×: Hana's board has 100 lanterns in a 10×10 grid. Right now 60 are lit. Next to it, the raffle wall has 100 hooks, and 7 of them have a winning tag. The crowd announcement needs both as percents.
map.Conceptual: percent means 'per hundred.': Conceptual: percent means 'per hundred.' Hana's board IS a hundred. So 'what percent is lit' means 'how many out of the hundred are lit.' Same for the raffle wall.
map.Procedural: when the whole is exactly 10: Procedural: when the whole is exactly 100, the count out of 100 is the percent number. Write the count and add the % sign. Do not slide any decimal. An answer like 0.something is the DECIMAL costume, and the announcement wants the percent.
map.Every stall pledged a share of its sales: Every stall promised a share of its sales to the pier. And every stall wrote that share a different way. Fractions. Decimals. Chaos.
map.The pier board only speaks percent. My t: The pier board only uses percent. My tea stall's tag says 9/20. Divide top by bottom: 9 ÷ 20 = 0.45. Slide the decimal two places: 45%.
map.Definition loaded: fraction → decimal →: Definition: fraction → decimal → percent are three outfits for one amount. Divide top by bottom for the decimal. Make it per hundred, with two decimal slides, for the percent. The amount never changes. Only the costume.
map.To rewrite a fraction as a percent: divi: To write a fraction as a percent: divide the numerator by the denominator. Then move the decimal point two places right and add the % sign. 9/20 = 0.45 = 45%.
map.Reader — the translator post is yours. T: Reader, the translator post is yours. Two hard tags are left. Turn them into percent so the whole market reads one language.
map.Two stubborn tags. Tag A pledges 13/20 o: Two hard tags. Tag A gives 13/20 of each sale to the pier. Tag B gives 0.08 of each sale. The market board only uses percent. Translate.
map.Conceptual: a fraction, a decimal and a: Conceptual: a fraction, a decimal and a percent are three costumes for ONE amount. The decimal is the bridge. Get it first. Then the percent is that same amount counted per hundred.
map.Procedural: Tag A — divide the top by th: Procedural: Tag A: divide the top by the bottom to get the decimal. Then slide the decimal point two places right for the percent. Tag B is already a decimal: read its HUNDREDTHS place, two slides right. Do not lose the zero after the point.
map.Tags translated, the crowd flows again —: The tags are done and the crowd moves again. It passes a stall with a sign still dripping wet paint.
map.Half off! HALF! You can't argue with hal: Half off! HALF! You cannot argue with half, junior leaguers.
map.Half of WHAT, Bram? Your shelf tag still: Half of WHAT, Bram? Your shelf tag still says 0.2 of the "regular" price. Your sign and your tag do not agree.
map.Tonight's mission is lanterns, not lawsu: Tonight's mission is lanterns, not lawsuits. VEX, log the gate stall. We will come back with proof.
map.The pier itself, dark beyond the lantern: The pier itself, dark beyond the lanterns. The repair plan splits it into 25 planks. Donations pay for them one by one.
map.Twenty-fifths don't speak percent yet —: Twenty-fifths are not percent yet, but 25 × 4 = 100. The snack stand paid for 6 planks. That is 6/25. Multiply top AND bottom by 4: 24/100. Twenty-four percent.
map.Scale the fraction to a hundred, then re: Scale the fraction to a hundred. Then read the percent right off. It is a free upgrade.
map.When the denominator divides 100 evenly: When the denominator divides 100 evenly (like 20, 25 or 50), scale the fraction to hundredths. Multiply top and bottom by the same number. Then the numerator is the percent. 6/25 = 24/100 = 24%.
map.Closing time. The mayor's big board wait: Closing time. The mayor's big board waits for the last announcement of the night. Bram waits to argue with it.
map.My stall pledged point-four of sales. Or: My stall gave point-four of sales. Or 4%. Same thing, of course. A small dot makes a small difference.
map.Reader — three locks. Ring the bell with: Reader, three locks. Ring the bell with TRUE numbers.
map.Boss Gate: turn the plank fraction into: Boss Gate: turn the plank fraction into a percent. Check Bram's brag. Pick the honest poster grid.
map.The mayor's board waits. Lock 1: the pie: The mayor's board waits. Lock 1: the pier banner says 19/25 planks are paid for. Post it as a percent. Lock 2: Bram says a 0.4 pledge and a 4% pledge are the same. Which is larger? Lock 3: next week's poster must show 30%. Pick Hana's honest grid.
map.Conceptual: Lock 1 — a percent needs a p: Conceptual: Lock 1: a percent needs a per-hundred view, and twenty-fifths scale to hundredths because 25 × 4 = 100. Lock 2: never compare a decimal with a percent in different costumes. Change one of them first. Lock 3: a grid only shows a percent when its WHOLE is exactly 100 parts. The shaded count alone proves nothing.
map.Procedural: Lock 1 — multiply the banner: Procedural: Lock 1: multiply the banner fraction's top AND bottom by 4. Then read the numerator of the hundredths. Lock 2: slide the decimal's point two places right to see its percent. Then compare. Lock 3: for each grid, count the shaded squares AND the total squares before you trust it.
map.Six planks to go. And that gate stall's: Six planks to go. And that gate stall's "50% off" still does not say 50% off of WHAT.
map.New distortion at the gate stall: a perc: A new distortion is at the gate stall: a percent hiding its whole. To be continued…
map.Percent.\"Per hundred.\" A rate out of 1: Percent."Per hundred." A rate out of 100. On a hundred-grid, the shaded count IS the percent. 60 lit lanterns out of 100 means 60%, and 7 out of 100 means 7%. No decimal point needed.
map.Fraction → decimal → percent.Three costu: Fraction → decimal → percent.Three costumes, one amount. Divide top by bottom for the decimal. Slide the decimal two places for the percent. 13/20 = 0.65 = 65%. The zero matters: 0.08 is 8%, not 80%.
map.Compare in one form.Never judge a decima: Compare in one form.Never compare a decimal and a percent in different costumes. 0.4 is 40%, ten times 4%. A grid only shows a percent when its whole is exactly 100 parts.
map.completed Unit 4 · Episode 1: Per Hundre: finished Unit 4 · Episode 1: Per Hundred and showed they know percents as rates per hundred and fraction–decimal–percent connections.
map.Thank you for lighting the board with th: Thank you for lighting the board with the crew. Episode 2 is already being built: half off, whole missing.
map.Different board — the test string Hana w: A new board: the test string Hana wired at home. 45 of its 100 bulbs glow. Percent means per hundred, so 45 out of 100 is 45%. The count and the percent match because the whole is 100.
map.Costume check: 45 out of 100 is also the: Costume check: 45 out of 100 is also the decimal 0.45. It is the same amount dressed differently. The % sign already means 'out of 100,' so the percent number stays 45, never 0.45.
map.Tiny counts work the same: 9 winning tic: Small counts work the same: 9 winning tickets out of 100 is 9%. Count, then %. That is the whole trick.
map.Your turn — same idea, different numbers: Your turn. Same idea, new numbers:
map.Different tag — the tea stall's 9/20. Di: A new tag: the tea stall's 9/20. Divide top by bottom: 9 ÷ 20 = 0.45. That is the decimal costume.
map.Decimal to percent: slide the point two: Decimal to percent: slide the point two places right. 0.45 becomes 45, so 9/20 = 45%. Same pledge, three outfits.
Watch the zero: the cocoa cart gave 0.06. Two slides right gives 6. Six HUNDREDTHS is 6%, never sixty. The zero between the point and the digit matters.
map.Different banner — the snack count read: A new banner: the snack count was 7/25 sold. Scale to hundredths: 7 × 4 = 28 and 25 × 4 = 100, so 7/25 = 28/100 = 28%.
map.Costume duel with different numbers: com: Costume duel with new numbers: compare 0.6 with 6%. Slide 0.6 two places to get 60%. The duel is over: sixty per hundred is far more than six per hundred. The decimal was the bigger amount in disguise.
map.Grid check: 20 shaded squares mean 20% O: Grid check: 20 shaded squares mean 20% ONLY if the grid has 100 squares. In a 40-square grid, 20 shaded is 20/40, one half, which is 50%. Count the whole before you trust the shading.
map.Post something first — both boards need: Post something first. Both boards need a number.
That is the DECIMAL costume, six tenths. The % sign already says 'per hundred,' so the percent number is the lit count out of 100. No decimal slide needed.
map.Look again — the board is exactly 100 la: Look again. The board is exactly 100 lanterns, and percent means per hundred. The lit count out of 100 IS the percent number.
map.That's the decimal — seven hundredths. T: That is the decimal, seven hundredths. The raffle wall wants the PERCENT: winners per hundred hooks.
map.The raffle wall holds exactly 100 hooks: The raffle wall has exactly 100 hooks. The winning count out of 100 is the percent.
map.Announcement posted! 60 of 100 lit is 60: Announcement posted! 60 of 100 lit is 60%, and 7 winners out of 100 hooks is 7%. Percent means per hundred. The board showed it all along.
map.Translate something first — three boxes: Translate something first. Three boxes wait for numbers.
map.That's the PERCENT costume in the decima: That is the PERCENT costume in the decimal box. This tag's decimal is between 0 and 1. Divide the top by the bottom.
map.Tag A's decimal: divide 13 by 20 — top b: Tag A's decimal: divide 13 by 20, top by bottom. Keep what the division gives you.
map.That's the decimal again — it already li: That is the decimal again. It is already in the first box. Slide it two places right to get the percent.
map.Decimal locked. Now slide its point two: Decimal done. Now slide its point two places right and add the % sign.
map.The zero matters — 0.08 is eight HUNDRED: The zero matters. 0.08 is eight HUNDREDTHS, not eight tenths. Eighty per hundred would be 0.80, a much bigger pledge.
map.That's the decimal it already wears. Per: That is the decimal it already has. Make it per hundred: slide the point two places right.
map.Tag B: read the hundredths. Two slides r: Tag B: read the hundredths. Two slides right. Watch the zero between the point and the 8.
map.Translated! 13/20 = 0.65 = 65%, and 0.08: Translated! 13/20 = 0.65 = 65%, and 0.08 = 8/100 = 8%. Three costumes, one amount. The market now reads one language.
map.Lock 1 first — the banner number leads t: Lock 1 first. The banner number leads the announcement.
map.Lock 1 holds. 19 is only the TOP of the: Lock 1 is shut. 19 is only the TOP of the fraction. It is out of 25, not out of 100. Scale the whole fraction to hundredths.
map.Lock 1 holds. That's the decimal costume: Lock 1 is shut. That is the decimal costume. The big board uses percent, per hundred.
map.Lock 1 holds. 25 × 4 = 100 — multiply BO: Lock 1 is shut. 25 × 4 = 100. Multiply BOTH parts of 19/25 by 4 and read the hundredths.
map.Lock 1 open! Lock 2: put both pledges in: Lock 1 is open! Lock 2: put both pledges in the SAME costume before you compare them.
map.Lock 2 holds. 4 looks bigger than 0.4 —: Lock 2 is shut. 4 looks bigger than 0.4, but slide 0.4 two places: it is 40 per hundred. Forty percent against four.
map.Lock 2 holds. That's Bram's exact claim: Lock 2 is shut. That is Bram's exact claim, and the bell says no. Slide 0.4 two places right. It is not 4 per hundred.
map.Locks 1 and 2 open! Lock 3: count shaded: Locks 1 and 2 are open! Lock 3: count shaded AND total squares in each grid. A percent grid must show its amount per HUNDRED.
map.Lock 3 holds. That grid lights 3 of 100: Lock 3 is shut. That grid lights 3 of 100. That is 3%. Ten times too small for the poster.
map.Lock 3 holds. Thirty squares glow, but t: Lock 3 is shut. Thirty squares glow, but that grid only HAS fifty. 30 out of 50 is 60%. Percent needs a hundred parts in the whole.
map.Lock 3 holds. 13 of 100 is 13% — not eve: Lock 3 is shut. 13 of 100 is 13%. Not even half way to the goal.
map.ALL LOCKS OPEN. 19/25 = 76/100 — the bel: ALL LOCKS OPEN. 19/25 = 76/100. The bell rings on 76% paid for. 0.4 is 40%, ten times Bram's 4%. Only the 30-of-100 grid truly says 30%. The market closes loud, and the pier fund glows.
Yes! Now go back and open that gate.
